top_choice_rationale: P001 awards Katori and Ye for the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock: a concrete invention (the lattice removes the trap-induced shift for a large neutral-atom ensemble) paired with a decisive realisation at the 1e-18 level, reproduced across several laboratories over two decades. The two-name allocation maps onto idea and realisation, and the citation scope is defensible. The distinctness from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes is a judgement I accept as a theorist outside atomic metrology, and credit beyond the pair remains an unverified limitation, but neither outweighs awarding a mature, well-attributed achievement over no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my own field is superconducting circuits and I have no documented link to the optical-clock groups
